🔵 [wdog-set-m-silent-unenforced] CUT/FOLLOW-UP On the no-setsid fallback (plain and detached-child), if `set -m` fails the worker lands in the dispatcher's pgid, `_watchdog_signal_worker` correctly refuses via the selfpg guard, but the run still reports `timeout_enforced: true` while nothing is bounded; consider setting a WATCHDOG_DISARMED flag in that branch and emitting `timeout_enforced: false`. Excluded: requires a host with neither setsid nor working job control, and the guard already satisfies the hard "never signal self" requirement.
🔵 [wdog-cgroup-no-fallback] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Cgroup path relies solely on `systemctl --user kill "$SCOPE_UNIT"` with `|| true`; a transient systemctl failure leaves the worker unbounded with no pgid fallback. Excluded: spec mandates the systemctl scope kill for this path and the unit exists synchronously before the earliest possible deadline.
🔵 [wdog-deadline-coincident-mislabel] CUT/FOLLOW-UP If the worker exits naturally in the same instant the sleeper fires, `.fired` is created before `wait "$rp"` returns and the run is stamped `timed_out: true` despite a natural exit (AGENT_EXIT is not consulted). Excluded: sub-millisecond coincidence, no process is harmed, sleeper is still reaped via the timed-out branch.
🔵 [manifest-timeout-dup-keys] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The base printf now always emits `timeout_seconds`/`timeout_source`; if `strict_manifest_fields` (not visible in this diff) still carries the pre-existing `timeout_seconds`/`timeout_source` for contract runs, strict-contract manifests contain duplicate keys (last-wins in node/jq, identical values). Excluded: cannot be confirmed from the diff and the contract suite is in the Verify list; drop the strict-side duplicates in a follow-up if present.
🔵 [output-comment-default-in-result] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The OUTPUT contract comment lists `"default"` as a possible result-JSON `timeout_source` value, but `emit()` only writes `timeout_source` when `TIMEOUT_SOURCE` is non-empty, so `default` only ever appears in the manifest. Excluded: documentation nit; the "(when present)" qualifier makes it non-misleading in practice.
